name: lap-stroke-trace
title: Lap Stroke Trace
description: A card whose backing texture is a genuine pitch-lap mirror-polishing stroke — a single continuously-extended polyline built from two superimposed rotations at an irrational (golden-ratio) frequency ratio so the path never closes or visibly repeats, its most recent 5s glowing brightest and the trailing 3s fading to nothing.
useWhen: a card whose backing texture should read as a single unrepeating trace being drawn live across a disc, where the mechanic's identity IS an irrational-ratio path that never closes and only a short recent window of it is ever visible. Pick honing-crosshatch instead when the texture should be many short discrete scratches at a FIXED angle turning over by population (birth/erosion of many independent strokes holding steady density), rather than one continuously-advancing polyline with a fading tail. Pick grinding-chatter-lobes instead when the surface itself should visibly deform into a growing wavy N-lobed rim profile (a loader-style process with a periodic dress/reset event), rather than a flat disc with a moving trace drawn across it.
instruction:
Build a card whose entire backing surface is a canvas-rendered pitch-lap optical-mirror polishing simulation, sourced from real optical-shop / amateur-telescope-making mirror grinding-and-polishing practice (Texereau, 'How to Make a Telescope'; Ceravolo stroke patterns), not a decorative rotating pattern. Root is a `rounded-[14px] border border-border bg-background` card holding an absolutely positioned, pointer-active, `aria-hidden` canvas filling the card behind a `pointer-events-none` content stack (heading, mono body copy, optional underlined link that re-enables `pointer-events-auto` and carries a `focus-visible` ring in `--ns-accent`).

Geometry is derived from the card's own smaller dimension via ResizeObserver: disc centre is the card centre, `discRadius = 0.42 * min(w,h)`, `strokeWidth = min(w,h) / 180`. The traced contact point is the sum of two rotating vectors, not a particle field and not a persisting grid: `point(t) = centre + A*(cos,sin)(2*pi*f_w*t + phaseW0) + B*(cos,sin)(2*pi*f_l*t + phaseL0)`, where `f_w = 0.05` Hz (workpiece rotation, slowed from real ~0.3-1 rev/s shop rates for card-scale legibility) and `f_l = f_w * phi^-1` (`phi^-1 = (sqrt(5)-1)/2 ~= 0.618`, the golden-ratio conjugate) — this irrational ratio is exactly what a real W-stroke/Prescott stroke achieves by combining workpiece spin with lap-arm throw, and it is what guarantees the path never closes or visibly repeats within any observation window. `A = 0.55 * throw`, `B = 0.45 * throw`, `throw = 0.78 * discRadius`. `phaseW0`/`phaseL0` are randomised once per mount (`mulberry32` seeded off `Date.now()`) so different page loads trace different arcs; this randomisation is explicitly NOT used for the reduced-motion path (see below), which must stay reproducible.

One point is appended to a trail array every animation frame — sampled at display rate, never at a coarser deposit threshold — tagged with `{x, y, t: simTime, angle: atan2(y-cy, x-cx)}`, where `simTime` is a locally-accumulated virtual clock that advances only while the rAF loop actually runs (paused/hidden cards don't age their trail). Every frame, points older than `TRAIL_HISTORY_S = 8` (by `simTime - point.t`) are dropped from the front of the array. Per-point brightness is age-based and NOT a flat fade: for `age <= 5` (`TRAIL_FADE_START_S`), brightness linearly decays from `1.0` (head) to `0.4` (`MID_BRIGHTNESS`, the 'peak trail luminance decays to 40% of head brightness by the fade point' spec value); for `5 < age < 8`, brightness linearly decays from `0.4` to `0`, then the point is dropped. Colour for a given brightness is a three-stop ramp, never a two-colour mix: `brightness >= 0.4` interpolates `midColor -> headColor`, `brightness < 0.4` interpolates `baseColor -> midColor`. Segments are drawn individually (`beginPath/moveTo/lineTo/stroke` per adjacent point pair) so each can carry its own alpha-equivalent colour; this is cheap at the ~480-point resident population 8s of 60fps sampling produces.

Colour tokens are read via `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)` for `--background`, `--ns-muted`, `--foreground` at mount and re-derived on a `MutationObserver` watching `documentElement`'s class — never a literal, and no paint happens before the first read. `baseColor` is always `--background`. Dark theme: `headColor = --foreground`, `midColor = --ns-muted` directly. Light theme (checked first, the harder case): `headColor = mix(muted, foreground, 0.85)`, `midColor = mix(muted, foreground, 0.4)` — bias/contrast retuned per the weld-pool convention (never inverted direction), so the disc stays a coherent value field in both themes. The disc's blank surface itself is filled with a faint radial gradient between `mix(base, mid, 0.05)` at centre and `mix(base, mid, 0.14)` at the rim (glass read, no hue), clipped to the disc circle. Chuck framing — an edge ring and a small centre dot, both derived from `mix(base, mid, 0.6)`, never `--border` used as a canvas stroke/fill (per the binding token rule, `--border` stays a DOM separator only) — is drawn after the clip is restored, so the ring sits crisp at the true disc edge regardless of trail content.

Interaction: pointermove over the canvas tracks `hoverAngle = atan2(y-cy, x-cx)` and drives a smoothed `hoverEnvelope` (exponential approach toward 1 while hovering, toward 0 once pointerleave/pointercancel fires, tau chosen so it settles within the spec's ~500ms decay). For each drawn segment, if `hoverEnvelope > 0` and the segment's stored angle is within `+/-15deg` of `hoverAngle`, its brightness is pulled toward `1.0` (head brightness) by `hoverEnvelope * falloff` (`falloff` a raised-cosine over the 15deg half-window) — this only ever raises brightness on the SAME base->mid->head colour ramp everything else uses, never mixes in `--ns-accent`, never changes `f_w`/`f_l` (which would read as the path skipping/glitching, an explicit reject), and never pauses `simTime`'s accumulation.

DPR-capped (max 2) backing store sized off the card's own `getBoundingClientRect`, rebuilt on `ResizeObserver` (which also recomputes `discRadius`/`strokeWidth`/`A`/`B` and re-triggers the static build if reduced-motion is active). The render loop pauses via `IntersectionObserver` (not scrolled into view) and `visibilitychange` (tab hidden), resuming via a `wake()` that only schedules a new rAF if one isn't already pending. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the trail is built once via a synchronous, deterministic zero-phase run (`phaseW0 = phaseL0 = 0`, ignoring the mount-random phases used by the live path) sampled at a fixed `dt = 1/60` from `t = 0` to `STATIC_T_S = 6.0`, pruned to the same 8s window, rendered once, named `FREEZE_PHASE = "half-lap"` and exposed as `data-reduced-motion-freeze` on the root; the loop never starts in this mode. No dependencies.
